slides.title: Protocol outline
bullets: Safety

slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: Solid-phase ELISA based on competitive binding: the microplate wells are coated with a monoclonal antibody to 25-OH D.
The sample is incubated with Release Reagent — 25-OH D is freed from vitamin D binding protein (VDBP) and binds to the antibody.
After washing, biotin-labelled 25-OH D (conjugate) and streptavidin-peroxidase (complex) are added; biotin-25-OH D competes with the sample’s 25-OH D.
After stopping, the TMB colour is read at 450 nm; its intensity is INVERSELY proportional to the 25-OH D concentration.

slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: 25-OH D is the major circulating metabolite and is what is measured to assess vitamin D status (active 1,25-(OH)2 D is about 1000-fold lower).

This protocol follows, as an example, the instructions for use of the Immusmol “25-OH Vitamin D (total) ELISA” kit (IFU MS E-5800, Version 11.0, 2024-08-02). The IFU of your laboratory’s own kit always takes precedence: other kits may use different volumes, times, factors and reference values.

slides.title: Specimen, kit contents and equipment
bullets: Specimen: serum or plasma (EDTA, lithium heparin or citrate). Do not use haemolytic, icteric or lipaemic specimens, or samples containing sodium azide.
Standards A–F: 0, 5, 15, 30, 60, 120 ng/mL (calibrated against DEQAS No. 548); controls 1 and 2 — values on the label/QC report.
Release Reagent, conjugate (biotin-25-OH D), complex (streptavidin-HRP), TMB substrate, stop solution (0.5 M H2SO4), 40× wash solution, 96-well break-apart plate.

slides.title: Specimen, kit contents and equipment
bullets: Equipment: calibrated microplate reader (450 ± 10 nm), calibrated micropipettes, 37 °C incubator, distilled or deionised water, absorbent paper, timer, graph paper or data-reduction software.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (microplate ELISA)
bullets: Bring all reagents and the strips needed to room temperature (21–26 °C) before use; mix without foaming.
Wash solution: dilute 30 mL of the 40× concentrate with 1170 mL of deionised water to 1200 mL; stable for 1 week at room temperature.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (microplate ELISA)
bullets: An opened kit keeps its activity for 8 weeks at 2–8 °C; store unused wells in the sealed foil pouch at 2–8 °C.
Do not mix components from kits with different lot numbers; use a new tip for each standard, control and sample.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (microplate ELISA)
bullets: This is not a semi-automatic photometric analyser test: a microplate reader and a 37 °C incubator are needed. Values come from the Immusmol “25-OH Vitamin D (total) ELISA” IFU (MS E-5800, Version 11.0); your own kit IFU takes precedence.

slides.title: Specimen storage and dilution
bullets: Serum: centrifuge venous blood at room temperature after complete clotting. Plasma: centrifuge blood in anticoagulant tubes immediately after collection.
Capped specimens keep up to 7 days at 2–8 °C; for longer (up to 12 months) freeze once at −20 °C. Invert thawed samples several times before testing.

slides.title: Specimen storage and dilution
bullets: Result above the highest standard: dilute with Standard A — 1:10 (10 µL sample + 90 µL Standard A) or 1:100 (10 µL of the 1:10 dilution + 90 µL Standard A); apply the dilution factor.

slides.title: Procedure rules
bullets: Each run must include a standard curve; once started, complete all steps without interruption.
Pipette samples and reagents in the same order and as quickly as possible at every step — this keeps the elapsed time equal in all wells.
Washing: briskly shake out the wells, wash 4 times and strike the wells on absorbent paper to remove droplets. Sensitivity and precision depend strongly on correct washing.
Do not let the wells dry after washing — add the next reagent immediately. Use a separate reservoir for the substrate.

slides.title: Procedure rules
bullets: Absorbance depends on incubation time and temperature: have the timer and the 37 °C incubator ready beforehand.

slides.title: Calculation and interpretation
bullets: Average the absorbance of each standard, control and sample; plot the standard curve (Y — absorbance, X — concentration). The IFU prefers a 4-parameter fit.
Read the sample concentration from the curve; samples above the highest standard (120 ng/mL) are diluted further or reported as such.
Units: 1 ng/mL = 2.5 nmol/L.

slides.title: Calculation and interpretation
bullets: Literature classification in the IFU: deficiency < 10 ng/mL (< 25 nmol/L); insufficiency 10–29 ng/mL (25–72.5 nmol/L); sufficiency 30–100 ng/mL (75–250 nmol/L); toxicity > 100 ng/mL (> 250 nmol/L).
IFU: each laboratory should establish its own reference range for its population; UV exposure, season, race and diet all affect 25-OH D.

slides.title: Performance and errors
bullets: Assay range 3.22–120 ng/mL; limit of detection (LoD) 3.224 ng/mL.
Cross-reactivity: 25-OH D3 99.50%, 25-OH D2 97.43% (total 25-OH D is measured); 1,25-(OH)2 D3 0.98%; 3-epi-25-OH D3 0.83%.
Main errors: incorrect washing, wells drying out, broken pipetting order or timing, contaminated substrate, uncalibrated pipettes or reader.
IFU: the result alone should not be the only reason for any treatment — correlate it with other clinical observations and tests.

slides.title: Quality control
bullets: Run normal and pathological controls with each standard curve.
Control values and ranges are in the QC report for the current lot — compare with them; take part in national or international quality assessment schemes.
If controls are out of range, patient results are invalid. Check pipettes and timer, reader, reagent expiry, storage and incubation conditions, washing.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: The stop solution contains 0.5 M H2SO4 — it may irritate and burn the skin; avoid contact.
TMB irritates skin and mucosa: if in contact, wash eyes with plenty of water and skin with soap and water.
Reagents made from human serum or plasma tested negative for HIV I/II, HBsAg and HCV, but treat them as potential biohazards.
Wear disposable gloves and never pipette by mouth; dispose of used reagents and materials as hazardous waste.
